name: ATI Inc.
moat_justification: Qualification-based moat: ATI's nickel superalloys, titanium, and forgings are certified into specific engine/airframe programs (requalification takes years), melt/forge capacity is scarce (20+ month lead times), and it is one of only three qualified Western producers of high-purity hafnium/zirconium, backed by long-term agreements, a record $4.4B backlog, and proven pricing power (Q2 2026 EBITDA margin +440bp YoY). Capped at 6 because through-cycle returns are poor (FY2020 net loss $1,572.6M, negative OE years within the last five), customers are a few powerful OEMs, and earnings ride the commercial aero cycle.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.1%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 2.15 vs 3-yr median 0.91 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
LOW_OE_YIELD: base OE yield 1.9% — valuation rests almost entirely on growth; tier is fragile
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Real qualification moat (6/10) and a record $4.4B backlog, but at $187.84 the price pre-pays a decade of flawless aero compounding — weighted IRR 5.3%, IV@15% $38.16; clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$38.
moat_for: Aero qualification / switching costs — materials certified per program, requalification takes years
Scarce melt/forge capacity — premium titanium lead times ~20 months, isothermal forging >24 months
One of only three qualified Western producers of high-purity hafnium and zirconium
Long-term agreements + record $4.4B backlog (+18% YoY); naval nuclear deal ~$1B over 5 years through 2030
Proven pricing power — Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 22.6%, +440bp YoY on price/mix
moat_against: Deep cyclicality — FY2020 net income -$1,572.6M; OE/share negative within the last five years
Customer concentration — a few airframe/engine OEMs with strong bargaining power
Capital intensity — FY2025 capex $280.6M vs D&A $168.1M, expansion capex through ~2028
Commodity input exposure (nickel, titanium) and rivals (Howmet, Haynes, Carpenter) adding qualified capacity
